open_points.subject: request and argument depth boundary
open_points.text: “the request message nests no deeper than `json_depth_max`” and “each JSON text a request carries as a string ... measured on its own, so the message around it adds nothing” versus “a run input value nested exactly `json_depth_max` deep is accepted”
open_points.question: Are values, constants, schemas and guard values always encoded as JSON text strings, or may they be native subvalues whose enclosing request levels make a value at `json_depth_max` fail the whole-message check?
options: Require these arguments to be JSON text strings and measure both the shallow outer message and each decoded text independently
Allow native JSON subvalues and let whole-message depth include their enclosing request structure
Exclude designated native argument subtrees from the whole-message depth calculation
open_points.default_guess: Require JSON text strings and measure the outer message and each embedded text independently.

open_points.subject: JSON text acceptance
open_points.text: “every JSON text it carries as a string canonical ... else `invalid_request`” versus A01 rule 1, which says the kernel computes canonical JSON and refuses values JCS cannot represent, and its required test accepts an exactly representable integer spelling without saying the supplied text must already equal JCS
open_points.question: Must an embedded JSON string already be byte-for-byte JCS, or is any parseable, JCS-representable text accepted and then canonicalized by the kernel?
options: Require the supplied text itself to equal its JCS serialization
Accept any representable JSON text and canonicalize it
Require canonical form only for selected embedded-text fields
open_points.default_guess: Accept representable JSON and canonicalize it, because content identities are computed by the kernel.

open_points.subject: common-check precedence for slot and flow purpose
open_points.text: A01 rule 5 says the purpose check comes “after the checks every request passes (A16 rule 1: size, token, schema, actor)”, while changed A16 rule 1 inserts whole-message depth and embedded-JSON canonicality/depth checks before actor authorization and operation checks
open_points.question: Do the new depth and embedded-JSON checks precede the purpose check, despite A01's exhaustive-looking parenthetical omitting them?
options: Apply every changed A16 common check before the purpose check
Apply only the four checks named by A01 before the purpose check
Treat embedded-JSON checks as part of schema but leave whole-message depth separately ordered
open_points.default_guess: Apply every A16 common check before any operation-specific purpose check.

open_points.subject: malformed JSON that also exceeds the depth ceiling
open_points.text: “The depth of a JSON value is ...” but depth is “measured ... before the message is parsed” and a deeper text is refused at its entry point
open_points.question: For text that opens more than `json_depth_max` containers but is not ultimately valid JSON, does the depth scan fail immediately, or must syntax validity be established first and the failure reported as malformed JSON?
options: Reject immediately when structural nesting crosses the ceiling
Validate syntax first, then calculate depth only for a valid JSON value
Use one indistinguishable invalid-JSON/depth refusal reason everywhere
open_points.default_guess: Reject immediately once structural nesting crosses the ceiling.

open_points.subject: function output depth measurement
open_points.text: “each value output of a function, as its own text” and “an output without canonical bytes [is counted] by the bytes of its text as returned”, while A03 defines `run` as returning Python objects rather than JSON texts
open_points.question: What exact text is depth-scanned and byte-counted for a Python output that cannot yet be canonically serialized, and is the returned output dictionary itself checked or only each member value?
options: The runner serializes each output member separately and checks each resulting text
The runner serializes and checks the complete returned dictionary
Depth is measured directly on Python objects and a separate rule defines byte counting when serialization fails
open_points.default_guess: Serialize and check each declared output member separately; treat the enclosing output dictionary only as the port container.

open_points.subject: older deep values used in new executions
open_points.text: “a lower `json_depth_max` bounds only what enters after it: every record stored under an earlier release — its values, constants and schemas — is read, executed with and returned as before” while rule 1 applies the current ceiling to “each value output of a function” and “a list the kernel assembles from mapped elements”
open_points.question: If an older stored value deeper than the new ceiling is passed to a function that returns it, or participates in a newly assembled mapped list, is the newly produced output grandfathered or refused under the current ceiling?
options: Grandfather only reads and surface returns; every newly produced output or assembled list uses the current ceiling
Grandfather data derived unchanged from an older stored value
Execute the entire old contract version under the depth ceiling of the release that issued it
open_points.default_guess: Apply the current ceiling to every newly produced function output and assembled list, even when derived from grandfathered records.
